title: Did adaptive execution switch the join?
prompt: This report should show that adaptive execution planned a sort-merge join for `shipments` and `warehouses`, then ran a broadcast hash join instead. It always says no broadcast ran. Fix `solve(shipments, warehouses)` so it returns one row with `rows`, `planned_sort_merge` and `ran_broadcast`.
rules: `rows` is the number of rows the inner join on `warehouse_id` returns.
`planned_sort_merge` is whether the plan before anything runs uses a sort-merge join. `ran_broadcast` is whether the final plan, the one that actually ran, uses a broadcast hash join.
Keep the settings at the top of the starter. Return the one row from `report`.
hints: Before an action runs, the plan text is only the first plan. Adaptive execution decides the rest while the query runs.
`joined.count()` runs a new counting query, not `joined` itself. `len(joined.collect())` runs `joined`, and afterwards its plan text shows what ran.
After the run, the text holds the final plan first, then `== Initial Plan ==`. Read the planned join before the action (or after that marker) and the final one before it.
explanation: Two things hide the switch. The starter reads the plan text before any action, when it's still the first plan. And `count()` doesn't run `joined`: it builds and runs a separate counting query, so `joined`'s own plan never becomes final. Read `before` first, run `joined` itself with `rows = len(joined.collect())`, then read the plan again and keep the part before `== Initial Plan ==`. On real data that's `True` and `True`. When `shipments` is empty, adaptive execution sees an empty side after the shuffle and replaces the join with an empty result, so neither join is in the final plan and `ran_broadcast` is `False`. The broadcast changes how the join runs, never which rows it returns.
